original_question: For the Gromov-Witten theory of a target variety X, prove that the full set of Virasoro constraints holds when X is an Enriques surface.
target_in_paper: Section (ii) "On the Virasoro constraints," Q3: "Prove the Virasoro constraints in case X is an Enriques surface."
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the mathematical theory involved (Gromov-Witten theory), the property to be established (the Virasoro constraints), and the specific target singled out by the paper (the Enriques surface).
missing_details: The paper states this as a concrete open problem for one fixed target, not as a general statement about an arbitrary target variety X; X should simply be taken to be an Enriques surface.
The nearby context ties the question to the Gromov-Witten invariants determined by the stable-map moduli spaces M_g(X, beta); this stable-map/Gromov-Witten setup is implicit in the draft.
To make the question stand alone, one should indicate that the claim concerns the full Gromov-Witten theory across all genera g and curve classes beta, not a single genus or class.
The ambient setting over C is implicit in the paper's general Gromov-Witten discussion; here the intended case is an Enriques surface in that algebro-geometric setting.
The phrase "full set" is not the paper's wording. The paper simply says "the Virasoro constraints," referring to the standard Virasoro constraints for Gromov-Witten theory cited in the literature.

The paper does not impose any extra homogeneity condition, degree restriction, operator nilpotency hypothesis, or "for sufficiently large" quantifier here, so none should be added in the refined version.
refined_question: Let X be an Enriques surface over C. Prove that the Gromov-Witten theory of X, determined by the stable-map moduli spaces M_g(X, beta) for all genera g and curve classes beta, satisfies the Virasoro constraints.
justification: The draft is aiming at the only Enriques-surface/Virasoro problem in the paper. In section (ii), page 2, the paper says that the spaces M_g(X, beta) determine the Gromov-Witten invariants of X, notes that the Enriques surface is a particularly interesting case where the Virasoro constraints are still unknown, and then formulates Q3 exactly as "Prove the Virasoro constraints in case X is an Enriques surface." The refined question keeps that exact scope, makes explicit the stable-map/Gromov-Witten framework and the all-genera/all-curve-class range already implicit in the phrase "the Gromov-Witten theory of X," and avoids broadening the problem beyond the paper's formulation or adding assumptions not present there.
